tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef, returning the complete-resource hash and byte pagination metadata.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef, returning the complete-resource hash and byte pagination metadata.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resource templates from every configured server.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

format.definition:
start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change_move: "*** Move to: " filename LF
change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resource templates from every configured server.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

tools.description:

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resource templates from every configured server.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `deepseek-v4-flash`: DeepSeek Responses Responses model Reasoning efforts: max, xhigh (default), low, high.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

Only call this tool for a concrete, bounded subtask that can run independently alongside useful local work; otherwise continue locally.
It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Optional number of turns to fork. Defaults to `all`. Use `none`, `all`, or a positive integer string such as `3` to fork only the most recent turns.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__novel_tools
tools.description: Tools in the mcp__novel_tools namespace.

tools.name: check_de_ai_minimality
tools.description: Deterministically reject de-AI rewrites that add content or flatten the original rhythm.

tools.name: check_timeline_feasibility
tools.description: Deterministically check whether travel between two timestamped events is physically feasible.

tools.name: connection_probe
tools.description: Deterministic no-op used only to verify a complete Responses tool loop.

tools.name: list_novel_resources
tools.description: List addressable novel resources. Pagination controls transport only and does not rank context importance.

tools.name: read_novel_resource
tools.description: Read a novel resource by resourceRef (chapters include .md, e.g. chapter:chapter-001.md), returning the complete-resource hash, exact chineseCharacterCount (CJK U+3400–U+9FFF), and byte pagination metadata. Use chineseCharacterCount for length checks; do not estimate from bytes.

tools.name: scan_de_ai_patterns
tools.description: Run the deterministic local Chinese de-AI pattern scanner on one resource. It does not call a model.

tools.name: search_novel_resources
tools.description: Search all matching novel resources without application-side context ranking.
